# C-101 Ammonia Screw Compressor: Control Narrative (Draft A)

**Module:** C-101. **Requirement IDs:** FR-C101-NNN. **Platform:** CompactLogix PLC, HMI in the engine room office.

Rules for this document:
- Prose holds no setpoint values. Every number is in the setpoint list (SP-nn) in the reply below.
- Values marked "confirm" are my provisional proposals. They are not from the owner.
- No instrument index, cause-and-effect chart or alarm database was supplied. Sections 2, 6 and 7 therefore hold that content in full.

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

C-101 compresses ammonia vapor from the suction header to the discharge header. The PLC starts, stops and protects C-101. The PLC also controls its capacity.

**Interfaces**
- Upstream: suction header (PT-101).
- Downstream: discharge system (TT-103). The condenser is outside this module.
- Machine room: XV-120, EF-201, AE-110A/B.
- Other compressors: receive the ESD signal.

**Safety functions.** The 150 ppm shutdown and the break-glass station may be safety functions. If so, the SRS owns them. This narrative states only the BPCS response (open item OI-03).

| ID | Requirement | FAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-001 | The PLC must run all C-101 control and trip logic. No control or trip function may depend on the HMI. | Disconnect the HMI with C-101 running. Confirm that control continues. Then simulate a low-oil trip and confirm that it trips. |
| FR-C101-002 | The break-glass station must stop C-101 through the starter control circuit. This must work with the PLC unpowered. | Remove PLC power. Push the break-glass station. Confirm that the SS-101 run circuit drops out. |

## 3. States and transitions

Automation level: A = automatic, OP = operator-prompted, M = manual.

| State | Entry condition | Allowed exits | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| ST0 Not Ready | PLC power-up, or any permissive false | ST1 | A |
| ST1 Ready | All permissives true (FR-C101-004) | ST2 (START), ST0, ST6 | OP |
| ST2 Starting | START pushed in ST1 | ST3 (sequence done), ST4 (STOP), ST5 (trip), ST6 | A |
| ST3 Running | Start sequence done | ST4 (STOP), ST5, ST6 | A (capacity auto or manual) |
| ST4 Stopping | STOP pushed in ST2 or ST3 | ST0 (motor stopped), ST5, ST6 | A |
| ST5 Tripped (latched) | Any C-101 trip in section 6 | ST0 (RESET, cause clear) | A |
| ST6 ESD (latched) | Gas shutdown or break-glass | ST0 (RESET, cause clear) | A |

| ID | Requirement | FAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-003 | The PLC must implement the state table. It must reject every transition not shown. | Command each invalid transition. Confirm that it is rejected. |
| FR-C101-004 | ST1 must need all of these: no latched trip, no ESD, and both AE-110 below SP-24. PT-101 must be above SP-12. ZT-105 must be at or below SP-11. SS-101 must have no fault. PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103 and ZT-105 must have good signals. The start count must be below SP-28. The SP-30 timer must be complete. | Make each condition false in turn. Confirm ST0 and the HMI shows the reason. |
| FR-C101-005 | START must be accepted only in ST1. | Push START in ST0, ST3 and ST5. Confirm no action. |
| FR-C101-006 | A start must count when the run command turns on. The window must be rolling. The count must block a start while the starts in the SP-29 window equal SP-28. | Make four starts. Confirm that the fifth is blocked. Confirm release when the oldest start leaves the window. |
| FR-C101-007 | The PLC must keep start times in retentive memory. If they are invalid at power-up, the PLC must assume the maximum starts at power-up time. | Cycle PLC power. Confirm that the count survives. Corrupt the data and confirm the lockout. |
| FR-C101-008 | RESET must leave ST5 or ST6 only when the trip cause is clear. | Press RESET with the cause active. Confirm no exit. Clear the cause and press RESET. Confirm ST0. |
| FR-C101-009 | After PLC power-up, C-101 must go to ST0. It must not start without a new START. | Cycle power with C-101 running. Confirm ST0 and no run command. |

## 4. Regulatory control

| Loop | PV | Output | Action | Modes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity (CC-101) | PT-101 | YY-106L / YY-106U pulses | PV above SP-01 plus SP-04: load. PV below SP-01 minus SP-04: unload. | Auto, Manual, Off |

Tuning is not in this document. Pulse parameters are SP-05 to SP-08.

| ID | Requirement | FAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-010 | In Auto and ST3, the PLC must pulse YY-106L when PT-101 is above SP-01 plus SP-04. It must pulse YY-106U when PT-101 is below SP-01 minus SP-04. | Ramp the PT-101 simulation. Confirm the correct solenoid pulses. |
| FR-C101-011 | Pulse width must scale linearly from SP-05 to SP-06 with the error beyond the deadband. The error for maximum width is SP-08. | Apply three errors. Measure the widths. |
| FR-C101-012 | The PLC must keep SP-07 between pulses. It must not pulse inside the deadband. | Hold PT-101 in the deadband. Confirm no pulses. Measure the interval. |
| FR-C101-013 | The PLC must not pulse YY-106L at SP-10 position. It must not pulse YY-106U at SP-09 position. | Simulate ZT-105 at each limit. Command each direction. |
| FR-C101-014 | While II-104 is at or above SP-21, the PLC must block load pulses in Auto and Manual. The block must clear below SP-21 minus SP-23. | Ramp II-104. Confirm the block and release. |
| FR-C101-015 | While II-104 is at or above SP-22, the PLC must pulse YY-106U in any mode. The unload must stop below SP-21. | Hold II-104 above SP-22. Confirm unload pulses in Manual. |
| FR-C101-016 | While TT-103 is above SP-19, the PLC must block load pulses. | Raise TT-103 above SP-19. Confirm the block. |
| FR-C101-017 | In ST2, the PLC must not pulse YY-106L. In Manual mode, the operator must pulse load and unload from the HMI. All blocks and trips must stay active. | Try to load in ST2 and in Manual with II-104 above SP-21. |
| FR-C101-018 | A mode change must not cause a pulse. In Off, ST0 to ST2 and ST4, the capacity loop must output no load pulse. | Change modes. Confirm that no pulse starts. |
| FR-C101-019 | Only a supervisor login may change SP-01. The PLC must reject values outside SP-02 to SP-03. | Enter values as operator and supervisor, inside and outside the range. |

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 Start sequence (SqBC, from ST1)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Check all permissives. Record the start time. | All true | Immediate | Return to ST0. Show the reason. |
| S2 | Pulse YY-106U until ZT-105 is at or below SP-11. Skip if already there. | ZT-105 at or below SP-11 | SP-31 | Return to ST0. Alarm ALM-C101-12. |
| S3 | Turn on the SS-101 run command. | SS-101 run feedback true | SP-32 | Remove run command. Trip T6. |
| S4 | Hold the PDT-102 and alarm bypass. Block load pulses. | SP-17 elapsed | SP-17 | Not applicable. |
| S5 | Enable PDT-102 protection. Go to ST3. | PDT-102 above SP-16 | SP-18 | Trip T2. |

FR-C101-020: The PLC must run steps S1 to S5 as written, with the timeout and failure response for each. Test: force each failure. Confirm the response and the state.

### 5.2 Stop sequence (from ST2 or ST3)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Pulse YY-106U toward SP-09. | ZT-105 at or below SP-11 | SP-31 | Go to P2. Alarm ALM-C101-12. |
| P2 | Turn off the SS-101 run command. | Run feedback false | SP-32 | Alarm ALM-C101-13. Keep the command off. |
| P3 | Start the SP-30 timer. Go to ST0. | Immediate | None | None |

FR-C101-021: The PLC must run steps P1 to P3 as written. A STOP in ST2 must skip P1 when ZT-105 is at or below SP-11. Test: STOP at full load, then STOP during start. Confirm the steps and the timeout response.

### 5.3 Trip and ESD response

FR-C101-022: On any trip in section 6, the PLC must turn off the SS-101 run command at once. It must not unload first. Go to ST5 or ST6. Test: trigger each trip. Confirm that the run command drops in the same scan.

FR-C101-023: If run feedback is still true after SP-35, the PLC must raise ALM-C101-14. Test: hold run feedback true after a trip. Confirm the alarm.

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

No cause-and-effect chart was given. These rows are the chart for C-101.

| ID | Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | PT-101 at or below SP-13 for SP-14 | Trip C-101 (ST5) | Latched | Operator RESET with PT-101 above SP-12 |
| T2 | PDT-102 at or below SP-16 for SP-18, after SP-17 | Trip C-101 | Latched | RESET, after C-101 is stopped |
| T3 | TT-103 at or above SP-20 | Trip C-101 | Latched | RESET with TT-103 below SP-19 |
| T4 | SS-101 fault | Trip C-101 | Latched | RESET after the SS-101 fault is cleared |
| T5 | Run feedback lost with run command on | Trip C-101 | Latched | RESET |
| T6 | Run feedback not true within SP-32 | Trip C-101 | Latched | RESET |
| T7 | Bad signal on PT-101, TT-103, or PDT-102 (see section 8) | Trip C-101 | Latched | RESET with good signal |
| E1 | Either AE-110 at or above SP-24 | Alarm. EF-201 to high speed. Block start. | Auto-reset. Both AE-110 below SP-26 | Automatic. EF-201 stops after SP-27. |
| E2 | Either AE-110 at or above SP-25 (voting per SRS; see OI-03) | ESD (ST6). Shut down all compressors. De-energize XV-120. EF-201 stays at high speed. | Latched | RESET after both AE-110 are below SP-26 and the PLC is reset |
| E3 | HS-121 pushed | Same effect as E2, except EF-201 (see OI-04) | Latched | Reset HS-121 at the station, then RESET at the HMI |

| ID | Requirement | FAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-024 | The PLC must implement rows T1 to T7 as written. | Trigger each cause. Confirm the effect, the latch and the reset. |
| FR-C101-025 | The PLC must implement E1. The PLC must not start EF-201 for a lone bad detector signal. | Raise one AE-110 above SP-24. Confirm EF-201 and the start block. Then reduce below SP-26 and confirm the SP-27 delay. |
| FR-C101-026 | The PLC must implement E2 and E3. XV-120 must stay closed until the operator opens it from the HMI after RESET. | Raise one AE-110 above SP-25. Press HS-121. Confirm all effects and that XV-120 does not reopen on RESET. |
| FR-C101-027 | The ESD output to the other compressors must be sent on E2 and E3. | Trigger E2. Confirm the output state. |
| FR-C101-028 | The soft starter protection (overload, phase loss) must stay in SS-101. The PLC only reads the fault. | Trip SS-101 by its test input. Confirm T4. |
| FR-C101-029 | The PLC must keep the first-out trip cause. The HMI must show it until RESET. | Trigger two trips. Confirm that the first shows. |

## 7. Alarms

No alarm database was given. Priorities are provisional (OI-08).

| Alarm ID | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALM-C101-01 | PT-101 below SP-12 | Medium | Check the suction valves and the system load. |
| ALM-C101-02 | PDT-102 below SP-15 (blocked during SP-17) | High | Unload C-101 manually. Check the oil system. |
| ALM-C101-03 | TT-103 above SP-19 | High | Unload C-101. Check the cooling and the oil. |
| ALM-C101-04 | II-104 above SP-22 | Medium | Check the loading. |
| ALM-C101-05 | AE-110A or B above SP-24 | High | Leave the room. Follow the plant emergency plan. |
| ALM-C101-06 | AE-110A or B above SP-25 (ESD) | Critical | Follow the plant emergency plan. |
| ALM-C101-07 | HS-121 active | Critical | Find the cause before you reset. |
| ALM-C101-08 | Trip T1 to T6, one alarm per trip | High | Read the first-out cause. Fix it. RESET. |
| ALM-C101-09 | Start blocked: start count at the limit | Low | Wait for the window. Do not bypass. |
| ALM-C101-10 | Bad signal: PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, ZT-105, AE-110A/B | High | Repair the instrument. |
| ALM-C101-11 | Bad signal: II-104 | Medium | Repair the instrument. |
| ALM-C101-12 | Slide valve did not unload within SP-31 | Medium | Check YY-106U and ZT-105. |
| ALM-C101-13 | Run feedback still true after the stop command | High | Open the SS-101 supply. |
| ALM-C101-14 | Run feedback still true after a trip | Critical | Open the SS-101 supply. |

FR-C101-030: The PLC must raise each alarm in the table on its condition and clear it when the condition is gone. Test: simulate each. Confirm the HMI text, and the acknowledge and clear behavior.

## 8. Abnormal handling

| ID | Condition | Required behavior | FAT test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-031 | A signal is below SP-33 or above SP-34 (bad PV) | PT-101, TT-103, PDT-102 bad: trip T7 (PDT-102 only after SP-17). ZT-105 bad: stop pulses, alarm, block start. II-104 bad: block load. AE-110 bad: ALM-C101-10. The bad AE-110 does not vote. The other AE-110 still votes. | Force each signal bad in Running and in ST0. |
| FR-C101-032 | Both AE-110 bad | Alarm. Start EF-201 at high speed. Block start. | Fail both detectors. Confirm the effects. |
| FR-C101-033 | HMI communication lost | The PLC keeps the state, the setpoints and the trips. Operator commands are unavailable. | Disconnect the HMI. Confirm C-101 holds state and trips. |
| FR-C101-034 | PLC power lost and restored | C-101 stops. Latched trips and the first-out cause stay in retentive memory. The PLC goes to ST0 or ST5 or ST6. There is no automatic start. | Cycle power in ST3 and ST5. |
| FR-C101-035 | PLC outputs lose power or the PLC faults | The run command goes off. XV-120 goes closed. YY-106L and YY-106U go off, and the slide valve holds position (confirm, OI-07). | Remove output power. Confirm each output. |

The fail positions of EF-201 and the slide valve are open items (OI-07).

## 9. Operator interface

The HMI shows on the C-101 faceplate:
- The state, the first-out trip cause, and the reason for ST0.
- PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104, ZT-105, and AE-110A/B.
- The start count and the time until the next start is allowed.
- The status of XV-120 and EF-201.

The operator can:
- Push START, STOP and RESET.
- Select Auto, Manual or Off.
- Pulse load and unload in Manual.
- Open XV-120 after RESET.

A supervisor can change SP-01.

| ID | Requirement | FAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-036 | START and RESET must show a confirm prompt: "Check the machine room is safe. Confirm START." and "Cause is clear. Confirm RESET." | Push each. Confirm the prompt and the cancel. |
| FR-C101-037 | The HMI must show the permissive that blocks a start. | Block each permissive. Read the text. |
| FR-C101-038 | The PLC must log each START, STOP, RESET, mode change and setpoint change with user and time. | Operate each. Check the log. |
